question: The students in a physics lab have been asked to measure the amount of electric current in a circuit. Which device should they use?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ammeter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ammeter** is a device used to measure the **electric current** flowing through a circuit.
 
• The unit of current measured by an ammeter is **ampere (A).**
 
• An ammeter is connected in **series** with the circuit to ensure that the entire current passes through it for accurate measurement.
 
• The internal resistance of an ammeter is kept **very low** to avoid any significant alteration in the circuit's current.
 
• Ammeter is widely used in **laboratories, industrial applications, and electrical troubleshooting** to measure current.
 
• Modern ammeters often use advanced technologies like **digital displays** for precise readings.
 
• An ammeter is a fundamental tool in understanding and analyzing **electric circuits**, especially in academic settings like physics labs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Altimeter**__

 __
 
• An **altimeter** is an instrument used to measure **altitude**, i.e., the height above sea level.
 
• It is commonly used in **aeronautics, mountaineering, and navigation** to determine elevation.
 
• The device works based on **air pressure**, as air pressure decreases with altitude.
 
• It is not related to measuring electrical current and hence cannot be used in a physics lab for this purpose.
 
 
 
• **Ohmmeter**__
 __
 
• An **ohmmeter** is used to measure **electrical resistance** in a circuit.
 
• Its unit of measurement is the **ohm (Ω).**
 
• This device is specifically designed to check the resistance of components, wires, or circuits.
 
• While it is useful for electrical testing, it is not appropriate for measuring **current**.
 
 
 
• **Voltmeter**__
 
 
• A **voltmeter** is used to measure the **voltage** or potential difference between two points in a circuit.
 
• It is connected in **parallel** to the component or circuit being measured.
 
• The unit of voltage measured by a voltmeter is the **volt (V).**
 
• While important in circuit analysis, it is not suitable for measuring **current**, which is the flow of charge.
